Case: Megan is a 75-year-old who presents to your primary care clinic with progressive neck and arm pain. The pain started 2 months ago and is primarily axial and exacerbated with neck movement. Megan denies any numbness or weakness, but has had difficulty with her balance and hand dexterity along with shooting pains down her arms. Your initial workup reveals severe cervical spondylosis with canal stenosis. Megan has never been in this much pain and is wondering what you can offer to relieve it.
Question: Would you offer hydrocodone to Megan? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
